dedupe_keys.name: leedr project home energy dataset 20 uk households

description: The LEEDR (Low Effort Energy Demand Reduction) dataset contains high-resolution monitoring of energy use in 20 UK family homes, collected to understand domestic energy consumption in everyday family life. The project was funded by the EPSRC from 2010 to 2014; the data are maintained by Richard Buswell in the Building Energy Research Group, School of Architecture, Building and Civil Engineering, Loughborough University, and were published in its repository in 2018 (updated 6 July 2018). Building surveys provide dimensioned plans, fabric and incoming energy information, images of key appliances and sensor locations, with documentation of calibration and processing; measurements include window and door opening, passive infrared room activity, electricity for the incoming supply and appliances, gas use and hot water use. Social science video data are held separately. Coverage: 20 households. Access: files and README in the Loughborough repository. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: a small sample, and the household locations are not given in the metadata read. Simulation uses: appliance and occupancy-driven demand models and validation of household energy simulations. Related records: REFIT smart home data and the Energy Demand Research Project.
